# SomerWalks snow guide (Somerville, MA)

> Somerville, Massachusetts' sidewalk snow and ice rules, for people who walk, roll or ride the bus. Made by the Somerville Pedestrian & Transit Advisory Committee (PTAC). This is not an official City of Somerville page: if anything here differs from the City, the City's rules apply. Official rules, in 9 languages: https://www.somervillema.gov/snow

Rules below were checked against the Somerville Code of Ordinances (Chapter 12 as amended by Ord. 2025-25, effective Dec 11, 2025; Sec. 1-11 effective Sep 24, 2026) and City and MBTA pages, in October 2026. Point people to the official sources for anything that matters to them, and say these details can change each winter.

## The sidewalk rule (Sec. 12-8)

- Clear snow and ice from the sidewalk within 6 hours of daylight after the snow stops. Only time between sunrise and sunset counts; the clock pauses overnight. Example: snow stops at 3 p.m. on Jan 15 → about 1.5 hours count that day, the rest after sunrise → clear by about 11:30 a.m. Jan 16. Snow stops overnight → clear by about 1 p.m.
- Applies after every snowfall, not only snow emergencies. Ice counts too.
- Path at least 36 inches (3 feet) wide, the whole length of the sidewalk, down to bare pavement. Where ice can't be removed, cover it with sand or similar.
- Who: "a person, including an owner, occupant, tenant, or agent, in charge of land or a building." Tenants and businesses renting space can be ticketed.
- Corner lots: both sidewalks.
- Curb ramps: buildings with commercial units must clear the abutting curb ramp through to the crosswalk (Sec. 12-8(a)(1), since Dec 2025). For homes this is a City request, not a legal requirement.
- The City can clear a neglected sidewalk and put a lien on the property (Sec. 12-8(c)).
- Don't let downspouts or roofs shed water onto the sidewalk (Sec. 12-2).

## Fines (Sec. 1-11)

- 1–3 unit homes: $100 first ticket, $200 second, $300 after.
- 4+ units and businesses: $150 first ticket, $300 after.
- Counted per season, October 1 to May 1. Unpaid fines can become a lien or block City licenses and permits.
- Shoveling snow into the street (Sec. 12-9): same fines. Only allowed in daylight on a day above 40°F, broken up and spread no more than 3 inches thick.
- Space savers (cones, chairs in the street): illegal under Sec. 12-18, $100, and the City can throw them out.

## Renting (State Sanitary Code, 105 CMR 410.260)

- Landlords keep shared exits, stairs and walkways clear; a lease can't change that. Tenants are responsible only for an exit that is theirs alone, and only if a written rental agreement says so.

## Snow emergencies (City of Somerville, winter 2026/27)

- Announced by City Alert (sign up: https://www.somervillema.gov/alerts) and flashing blue lights at 22 major intersections.
- 4 hours to park on the even-numbered side of the street. Wrong side: $100 ticket and a possible tow.
- Free parking in 13 City lots (https://www.somervillema.gov/snow/off-street-parking); Tufts Dowling Garage free for Ward 6 and 7 residents who register with Tufts. Never a school lot.
- After it ends: leave City lots within 2 hours; resident permit rules return after 24 hours; dig your car out within 48 hours.
- Towed: Stephen's Towing, 781-395-0808, pickup at Dilboy Stadium, 110 Alewife Brook Pkwy. $132 tow + $35/day storage, plus the $100 ticket.

## Bus stops and transit

- The City clears most of its 281 bus stops after the streets. The MBTA clears all route 109 stops, plus some on 77 (Mass Ave) and 104 (Sullivan Square), within 24 hours after snow ends. Property owners clear the sidewalk leading to the stop.
- Uncleared stop: call 311; for 109, 77 or 104 stops, tell MBTA Customer Support.
- Check service at https://www.mbta.com/winter. Routes 85 and 93 may run snow routes.
- The Community Path is cleared by the City but can close in big storms.

## Ice melt (Minnesota Pollution Control Agency guidance, not a City rule)

- Works down to (pavement temperature): rock salt 15°F, magnesium chloride −10°F, calcium chloride −20°F, calcium magnesium acetate 20°F. Sand gives grip but melts nothing.
- Shovel first; use a little melt (about 12 oz covers 10 sidewalk squares) and sweep up leftovers.

## Report or get help

- Report an icy or unshoveled sidewalk: 311, or 617-666-3311, the 311Somerville app, or 311requests@somervillema.gov.
- Seniors and people with disabilities can book a teen shoveler before the storm: 617-625-6600 x2321.

- [Cards](https://somerwalks.org/snow/cards.html): 34 shareable phone-size cards
- [Source code and research](https://github.com/vitorpamplona/somerwalks): ordinance text, sources, open questions for officials
